subject: maths
question:
The volume of a solid hemisphere is 19,404 cm³. Its total surface area (in cm²) is:

(Take π = frac{{ {22} }}{7})
solution:
__Shortcut Trick__

Volume = (2/3) × π × r³ = 19404

⇒ r³ = 19404 × (21/44) = 441 × 21 ⇒ r = 21 cm

TSA of solid hemisphere = 3 × π × r²

⇒ TSA = 3 × (22/7) × 21 × 21 = 66 × 63 = 4158 cm²

**∴ The correct answer is 4158 cm².**

**__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Volume of solid hemisphere = 19,404 cm³

π = 22/7

**Formula Used:**

Volume of hemisphere = (2/3)πr³

Total surface area (TSA) of solid hemisphere = 3πr²

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/d6ce71a7946324f3e944689bee14b49154d14a826b2bea79bfcd155d9f8f09e0.png] 

**Calculations:**

⇒ (2/3) × (22/7) × r³ = 19404

⇒ (44/21) × r³ = 19404

⇒ r³ = (19404 × 21) ÷ 44

⇒ r³ = 441 × 21

⇒ r³ = 21 × 21 × 21

⇒ r = 21 cm

Now, calculate Total Surface Area (TSA):

⇒ TSA = 3 × π × r²

⇒ TSA = 3 × (22/7) × 21 × 21

⇒ TSA = 3 × 22 × 3 × 21

⇒ TSA = 66 × 63

⇒ TSA = 4158 cm²

**∴ The correct answer is 4158 cm².**

**__Additional Information__**

Curved Surface Area of Hemisphere

The curved surface area of a hemisphere (excluding the flat base) is given by 2πr².

Volume and Surface Area of a Sphere

For a full sphere, Volume = (4/3)πr³ and Total Surface Area = 4πr².

Relationship between Sphere and Hemisphere

A solid hemisphere has a flat circular base, which is why its TSA (3πr²) is more than half of a sphere's surface area (2πr²).</p
